dominance_assessment: No single dominant gap: TWO materially independent systemic axes dominate — (A) evidence-layer currency/authority semantics (G1+G3+G4, explains stale/current criticals and zero-source honest/relit choices) and (B) interaction-layer task-type routing (G2, explains #26/#27/#31 residuals) — plus one trust axis (G5) and one reliability axis (G6). Axes A and B fail in different pipeline stages with disjoint case populations (A: troubleshooting/commercial narratives; B: no-model/scenario/greeting inputs).

gaps.statement: The answering stage lacks reliable current-vs-historical evidence semantics: case documents, historical quotes and authoritative current pages compete in one context with no temporal/authority ordering, and no marking survives into generation.

Task-type routing is decided by surface-form gates (verbatim social patterns, substring deixis, four-label intent) that cannot distinguish 'product unclear' from 'scenario/recommendation task' and cannot escalate domain-adjacent questions to retrieval-with-clarification.

Citation integrity validates numeric presence, not claim-source correspondence or currency: a stale claim can acquire a legitimate-looking citation to a current page whenever its numbers appear anywhere in that page.

Retrieval selection has no authoritative-source preference for narrative/troubleshooting phrasing: symptom-similar internal case documents outrank (or displace) existing authoritative spec pages, and the public-vs-background split is invisible to selection quality.

The background channel (internal case documents) participates in generation with identity-bearing content and no provenance shown to the user; PII redaction exists only on the user's own message, and suppression of case identities is prompt-level rather than deterministic.
Response strategy (answer vs bound refusal vs background relay) is unstable across identical-intent runs; reliability of any single-run outcome is not guaranteed by the pipeline.
The corpus lacks third-party/competitive knowledge entirely; ecosystem questions admit only bounded refusal.

Zero-source outcomes are structurally invisible to users: the sources event hides the internal evidence actually used, so answers can cite nothing while asserting case-derived specifics (or refuse) without the user learning why.
